summary: Treated the 5-minute budget as a compute-allocation problem and changed only three constants in train.py. Halving the global batch from 2^19 to 2^18 tokens was worth -0.0116 val_bpb (the baseline was step-starved), and widening the model at fixed depth 8 from dim 512 to 640 to 768 (ASPECT_RATIO 96, 6 heads x 128) was worth a further -0.0180, partly because wider matmuls raise MFU from ~35% to ~44% so fewer tokens still buy more useful compute. What did not work: pushing the batch down to 2^17 at dim 512 (+0.006) and head_dim 64 instead of 128 (+0.009, purely a throughput loss - MFU fell to 28%). Width gains are clearly flattening (-0.0147 then -0.0033), and peak VRAM at dim 768 is only 33GB, so the next things I would test are dim 896 and depth 10 at dim 768 to find where the size curve turns, plus an LR retune (matrix_lr, embedding_lr) at the new width since the LRs were tuned at dim 512 and only rescaled by the built-in 1/sqrt(dmodel) rule.
